title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's notational set-up for étale fundamental groups in the Long March notes. He writes E_X for the fundamental group (groupoid) of X and E_X^ξ for the profinite group at a 'point' ξ.

Step 1, eq. (6). The functoriality E(f): E_X -> E_Y of the previous page, for f: X -> Y, is made precise as an actual (effective) homomorphism of profinite groups E_X^{X~} -> E_Y^{Y~}. The base points are not geometric points but universal (pro-)coverings. X~ is a universal pro-cover of the connected scheme X. The composite X~ -> X -> Y factors through a universal pro-cover Y~ of Y, and this determines Y~.

Step 2. Grothendieck remarks that one should really write E_Y^{X~}. More generally one should write E_Y^Z for any 1-connected Y-scheme Z (connected and simply connected), because such a Z acts as a fibre functor on the classifying topos of finite étale covers of Y. In modern terms: for T finite étale over Y, the pullback T x_Y Z is a completely split cover of Z. So T |-> pi_0(T x_Y Z), equivalently T |-> Hom_Y(Z, T), is a fibre functor. E_Y^Z is its automorphism group, and E_Y^{X~} = E_Y^{Y~} canonically.

Step 3, eq. (7). (X, X~) |-> E_X^{X~} is a functor from the category of connected schemes equipped with a universal cover (or just with a 1-connected Z mapping to X) to profinite groups. It specialises to the category of geometrically pointed schemes (X, ξ).

The next page continues with (8)-(9): geometric points of X push forward to geometric points of Y. It then defines the relative group E_{X/Y} as the kernel of E_X -> E_Y, which is the setup for the homotopy exact sequence. The whole page serves to fix rigorous base-point conventions for anabelian and Teichmüller-tower considerations.
errors: Grothendieck writes 'le topos B_{pi(X)} des rev. étales de Y'. It should be B_{pi(Y)}, the topos of étale covers of Y. This looks like a slip of the pen.

Minor gap: for X~ -> Y to determine Y~ one needs a universal pro-cover of Y. The factorisation of X~ -> Y through it is unique only once the pro-cover structure is fixed. This is standard (SGA1 V) and harmless.

ideas.what: Use universal pro-coverings instead of geometric points as base points, giving a strict functor from 'universally covered' connected schemes to profinite groups.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group with base point a universal pro-étale cover (pro-representability of the fibre functor)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V (pro-representability of fibre functors, universal covering)

ideas.what: Any simply connected Y-scheme Z defines a fibre functor on finite étale covers of Y, giving a group E_Y^Z; a generalised base point.
ideas.modern_name: Generalised / 'fat' base points; fibre functor attached to a simply connected scheme over Y (cf. Deligne's tangential base points, base points in anabelian geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in SGA1. Tangential base points: Deligne (1989). Used widely in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Ihara, Mochizuki)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA1 V; La Longue Marche discusses base points and 'paquets de points base'

ideas.what: Relative fundamental group as the kernel of E_X -> E_Y (set up for the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Geometric fundamental group / homotopy exact sequence

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful notational and base-point conventions (universal covers or 1-connected schemes as base points). They are standard since SGA1 and common in anabelian geometry; nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: 'pour le topos B_{pi(X)} [?] des rev. étales de Y' should read 'le topos B_{pi(X)} des rev. étales de Y...)', with the '[?]' removed. Mathematically pi(Y) is meant.
The crossed-out word before the inserted E_X^{X~} after 'On peut dire que' is illegible. The insertion above it looks like 'E_X^{X~}' (possibly a variant superscript).
'au regard de la cat.' may read 'en regard de la cat.'
